study_id: Tian et al. - 2023 - Machine Learning-Based Prognostic Model for Patients After Lung Transplantation

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study involves adult lung transplant recipients and uses a random survival forests machine learning model to predict post‑transplant survival, meeting all population, intervention, outcome, and study design criteria.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: National Natural Science Foundation of China
identification_methods.Setting: Single-center retrospective prognostic study at Wuxi People’s Hospital affiliated to Nanjing Medical University
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective prognostic study using random survival forests to predict overall survival after lung transplantation
identification_methods.Institution: Wuxi People’s Hospital affiliated to Nanjing Medical University
identification_methods.Address: Wuxi Lung Transplant Center, Wuxi People’s Hospital affiliated to Nanjing Medical University, 214000 Wuxi, China
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Clinical records from Wuxi People’s Hospital (single-center)
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult patients >18 years who underwent lung transplantation; excluded retransplant, pediatric cases, and those with severe missing data
identification_methods.Input Variables: 22 clinical characteristics (4 recipient, 1 donor, 4 procedural, 13 post‑transplant); 16 variables selected for final RSF model
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Multiple imputation by chained equations using the ‘mice’ R package
identification_methods.Validation Method: Hold‑out validation with 7:3 train‑test split; internal test set and subgroup analyses
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Feature selection via variable importance with bootstrapping (1000 repetitions); hyperparameter tuning by grid search; performance assessed using integrated AUC, integrated Brier score, and calibration; internal validation on test set and subgroup validation

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult patients (>18 years) who underwent lung transplantation between January 2017 and December 2020 with complete follow-up records
population.Exclusion criteria: Retransplantation (6 patients), pediatric lung transplant (7 patients), severe missing data (6 patients)
population.Population Notes: Patients randomly assigned to training (353) and test (151) sets in a 7:3 ratio; both single and double lung transplants included

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Tabular clinical variables (22 pre- and post-transplant characteristics)
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data used for time-to-event prediction
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Grid search hyperparameter tuning; bootstrapping for VIMP; internal validation with hold‑out test set
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome was overall survival; secondary time‑point predictions at 1 month and 1 year
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Focus on RSF performance versus Cox regression benchmark
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: Integrated area under the curve (iAUC) and integrated Brier score (iBS)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All lung transplant recipients in the test set
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Integrated AUC over 1–48 months on held‑out test cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: RSF outperformed Cox; stratified patients into low‑ and high‑risk groups with mean OS 52.91 months vs 14.83 months
